'''Keijo Olavi Kajantie''' (born 1940) is a Finnish theoretical physicist and Professor and Adjoint Scientist at the [[Helsinki Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.hip.fi/?page_id=267 |title=Helsinki Institute of Physics personnel |access-date=2020-01-11 |archive-date=2019-12-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230221318/http://www.hip.fi/?page_id=267 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was Professor of Physics at the [[University of Helsinki]] from 1973 to 2008.<ref>Facta2001, WSOY 1981, Volume 7, paragraph 447</ref><ref name="acadsci"/> From 1985 to 1990 he was a Research Professor of the [[Academy of Finland]]<ref>WSOY Iso Tietosanakirja Part 3., p. 129, WSOY 1995</ref> and he has worked in the CERN Theory Division.<ref name="Home page of Keijo Kajantie">[https://www.mv.helsinki.fi/home/kajantie/ Home page of Keijo Kajantie]</ref> He is best known for his contributions to the study of the [[Electroweak interaction|electroweak]] and [[Strong interaction|strong]] interactions at high temperatures, as well as to the field of [[High-energy nuclear physics|ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions]].<ref>[https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/K.Kajantie.1 Scientific publications of Keijo Kajantie] on [[INSPIRE-HEP]]</ref> His research interests include ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions, [[finite temperature field theory]], [[string theory]] and [[QCD matter]], [[cosmological phase transitions]] and [[null infinity]] in general relativity.<ref name="Home page of Keijo Kajantie"/>

==Honours and awards==
Kajantie was awarded the Finnish Academy of Science Award in 2008<ref name="acadsci">[https://www.acadsci.fi/en/scholarships-and-prizes/academy-award/former-recipients.html Finnish Academy of Science Award Former Recipients]</ref> and the Order of the Lion of Finland in 2012.<ref>[http://www.hs.fi/kotimaa/a1354538752297 Highest decorations awarded by the President of the Republic], ''Helsingin Sanomat Uutiset Kotimaa'' <span style="font-size: 1em; line-height: 1.5em;">4.12.2012, v</span>dated 13.1.2014</ref>
